correctness.rationale: For κ_i>0 the two-sided stationary stochastic convolution exists uniquely and is bounded in conditional variance by D/κ_min. At entry to phase i, fresh A_i is independent of inherited position. Ito conditional second moment gives b_{3-i}=q_i+(b_i-q_i) ℓ_i and the displayed solved b. The future attenuation integral after a fresh entry is H_i=h_i+g_iH_{3-i}, with unique solution since 0<g_1g_2<1. Conditional on age u and current holding length a, the conditional coordinate second moment is q_i+(b_i-q_i)e^{-2κ_i u}; integrated future response is (1-e^{-κ_i(a-u)})/κ_i+e^{-κ_i(a-u)}H_{3-i}. Campbell/alternating renewal reward averages their product over u∈[0,A_i] divided by T, yielding M_i and J_i and the exact I formula. Independence of future Brownian increments proves C(s)=E[X_0² exp(-∫_0^sκ_{J_v}dv)] and positivity allows Tonelli; κ_min>0 gives integrability. Stationary Itô balance yields potential energy D/2; two jump-work rewards give (κ_1-κ_2)(b_1-b_2)/(2T). value.rationale: For a standard switched harmonic trap, occupations, state-conditioned variance, average potential energy and switching work are physical inverse observables. Their inability to identify low-frequency position fluctuations is a motivated, exact observability boundary. The same-mean, same second-rate-transform witness cleanly isolates a genuinely independent first-rate Laplace signature and shows a researcher why temporal spectra are needed in addition to static/energetic measurements. The explicit nonzero rational spectral gap is not a trivial normalization or a random arbitrary slice; it exhibits a structural difference between one-time second moments and two-time linear response. No general full-spectrum theorem or paper-sized contribution is required for this standalone exact counterexample.
